commitResults.messageTitle: Add date-time parsing and resilient storage loading
commitResults.messageBody:
Store deadline and event timestamps as LocalDateTime values, accept ISO-style date and time input, and render them in a friendly format.

Validate impossible dates and reversed event ranges. Preserve startup when saved data is malformed by skipping corrupted records while loading valid tasks.

Expand UI persistence tests to cover valid and invalid date handling, legacy records, corrupted data, and delimiter-safe storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-7: add date-time parsing and resilient storage
commitResults.messageBody: Integrate typed deadline and event timestamps, date validation, corruption-tolerant data loading, and expanded UI coverage into master.

Accept d/M/yyyy dates with optional HHmm times alongside the existing ISO formats, allowing commands such as 2/12/2019 1800 while preserving the unambiguous storage format.

Update UI coverage for slash-formatted dates, impossible dates, and clearer format guidance.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-8: support flexible date input
commitResults.messageBody: Integrate day/month/year date parsing alongside ISO formats so Pathfinder understands inputs such as 2/12/2019 1800 while retaining strict validation and compatible storage.

Move standard-input reading, separators, greetings, responses, task-added feedback, and the farewell out of Pathfinder into a cohesive Ui class.

This reduces Pathfinder's presentation responsibilities while deliberately preserving its current command orchestration, keeping the first OOP extraction small and behaviour-compatible. All nine Java 25 UI cases pass unchanged.

Move command-word normalization, argument validation, task-number parsing, and todo, deadline, and event construction out of Pathfinder into a stateless Parser class.

Keep command execution and persistence in Pathfinder for this increment, creating a stable parsing boundary for the upcoming Command hierarchy without changing console behaviour. All nine Java 25 UI cases pass unchanged.

Move Pathfinder classes beneath the pathfinder base package, grouping parsing, storage, tasks, UI, utilities, and exceptions by responsibility while retaining src/main/java as the source root.

Update imports, IntelliJ setup documentation, and the UI test configuration. Teach the test runner to discover packaged sources recursively and launch the fully qualified main class. All nine Java 25 UI cases pass unchanged.

Point the Gradle application plugin at pathfinder.Pathfinder and rename the Shadow JAR from duke.jar to pathfinder.jar so the packaged application uses the project's actual entry point and identity.

Verified with JDK 25 using both gradlew build and an interactive gradlew run session.

Add focused tests for command parsing, date-time conversion, and task persistence, including invalid inputs, boundary cases, legacy data, and corrupted records. Document the project policy to maintain JUnit coverage for the highest-value methods after code changes.

Describe every public class, constructor, and method, including parameters, return values, and failure conditions. Document non-trivial private parsing, persistence, and command-handling helpers so generated API documentation explains the design and behavioral contracts.

Several classes use inconsistent naming, mutable fields, and formatting
that does not follow the project coding standard.

Rename ToDoTask to TodoTask, clarify task field and collection names,
make unchanging fields final, and align switch cases and imports with
SE-EDU conventions. Add missing API comments so the code is easier to
read and maintain without changing behavior.

Update affected parser and storage tests to use the corrected class
name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add SE-EDU Java coding standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Java changes need a consistent source of project-specific style rules.

Add a project skill that summarizes the SE-EDU standard and links to
the authoritative guide. Require agents to invoke it for production
and test Java changes so future edits remain consistent.

Commit and branch conventions need a shared project-specific source.

Add a project skill that defines compliant subjects, explanatory
bodies, and branch names. Require agents to invoke it before proposing
or creating commits so repository history remains clear.
Allow users to find tasks using case-insensitive description keywords. Handle missing keywords and no-match results with Pathfinder-style feedback, and cover the behavior with JUnit and UI tests.
Bring the documented Pathfinder APIs into master so public classes and non-trivial methods are easier to understand and maintain.

Apply SE-EDU Java conventions across production and test code.

Add project-specific Java and Git skills.

Require future code and commits to follow those standards.

Master lacks the Level 9 task-search feature.

Add case-insensitive description search and its automated tests.

Keep the feature history visible with a non-fast-forward merge.
